newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A rush of exporter dollar selling thwarted initial attempts to push the rand weaker on Wednesday as the South African currency extended its rally against the U.S. unit.
At the 1400 GMT finish, the rand was pegged at 4.5590/5640 against the dollar from 4.5645/5675 overnight after trading in a range of 4.5525 to 4.5760 bid on the day.

Dealers initially expected the rand to weaken in line with a softer bond market, calling the currency overbought and in need of a correction after firming 15 cents against the dollar so far this year.
It weakened to 4.5760 before exporter selling emerged, driving the rand to its intraday high of 4.5525 by 0920 GMT.
"We saw some heavy exporter interest and then the foreigners jumped on the bandwagon," a trader said.
In the lower 4.55 area, importers surfaced and, coupled with pressure from local profit-taking, the rand moved weaker to trade in a tight 4.5560 to 4.5630 range for the rest of the afternoon.
"The rand seems to have found a bit of a level around 4.56," a trader said. "We might be in for a bit of a correction but the trend is definitely still down."
The key 4.55 level, cited by various dealers as a key chart level to break, was expected to be tested by Monday next week.
The currency retraced some of its recent gains against sterling to trade at 7.4032/4103 against sterling from 7.3370/3353 on Tuesday and at 0.3593/3598 marks from 0.3613/3623 marks previously.

The bond market also had a volatile day, trading between a high of 15.53 percent and a low of 15.365 percent before settling at 15.41 percent -- little changed from its overnight 15.40 percent finish.
Dealers said that an initial overhang of stock following New York-based profit-taking moved the market into territory where both offshore and local quality buying emerged.
"It started off with a bit of selling by a couple of players who felt the market was overbought," a dealer said. "But in the high 15.40s and above the 15.50s we saw some quality buying."
In the afternoon session, local jobber profit-taking pulled yields off their intraday lows.
"Today a lot of excess stock has been taken out of the market...once the jobbers are out of the way and have taken their profits the quality buyers will return," the dealer said.
"I think we will make a concerted effort to move to the 15.30 percent level on Thursday," he added.
On the money market, the continued easing in liquidity helped rates lower while surprising dealers accustomed to month-end pressure pushing the shortage up.
The Reserve Bank said the shortage fell to 8.937 billion rand on Tuesday from 9.842 billion rand on Monday.
Roelf du Plooy, the Reserve Bank's assistant general manager of money and capital markets, said the lower shortage was primarily a result of foreign exchange flows.
"At the moment (commercial) banks are selling dollars back to the Reserve Bank...in quantities much larger than we expected them to," du Plooy said.

Three-month NCD rates fell to between 17.05 to 17.20 from 17.10 to 17.25 percent on Tuesday, while the 90-day BA rate was slightly lower at between 16.35 to 16.55 percent from 16.40 to 16.60 percent previously.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners were net sellers of 3.41 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 304.83 million rand on Monday.
Nominal cumulative turnover on the bond market on Tuesday was 6.49 billion rand from 8.9 billion rand on Monday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
